propositions: Mutation testing shards require phased enforcement modes (advisory, ratchet, strict) with evidence-driven promotion, not blanket score ceilings, to prevent normalization of real contract gaps while accommodating stale historical counts.

Shard selection must map changed source, tests, and support files to their behavioral cores; promotion to ratchet requires three stable base/head pilot runs ≤24 minutes; promotion to strict requires all survivors individually fingerprinted or mutants killed.

Execution uses fresh isolated base/head archives with no persisted verdict cache, pinned mutmut 3.7.0, max-children=1, per-shard 30-minute job timeout, and timeout_constant=1.0 and timeout_multiplier=15.0 derived from .github/mutation-shards.toml.

Advisory mode runs head only and reports survived/no-tests/timeout findings nonblocking but blocks missing, zero-mutant, incomplete, or unrecognized evidence; ratchet preserves unchanged legacy outcomes and blocks killed-to-survived regressions; strict requires every mutant killed or individually reviewed equivalent.

Selector emits JSON, supports exact Gerrit patchset checkout with vote.needs wiring, generates per-shard matrix jobs, weekly/manual all-shard sweeps, and fails on unresolved refs while treating empty selection as explicit success.
